questions.question: What is a line of symmetry? Use a folded paper heart to explain.
questions.expected_answer: A line of symmetry divides a shape into two halves that match exactly when the shape is folded along the line. The paper heart is cut on a fold, so the fold line runs down its middle and the two halves fit exactly on top of each other.

questions.question: How many lines of symmetry does a square have, and how many does a rectangle have? Explain the difference.
questions.expected_answer: A square has 4: up and down, across, and the two diagonals. A rectangle has only 2: up and down and across. Its diagonals are not lines of symmetry, because folding along them puts a long side on a short side.

questions.question: A corner is 4 squares to the left of an up-and-down line of symmetry. Where is its partner?
questions.expected_answer: Its partner is 4 squares to the right of the line, on the same row, directly across from it.
